the study of physiological parameters associated with thermal stresses in small ruminant species (goats and sheep), under tropical climate conditions, in order to improve their productivity and welfare.
the effect of different nutritional strategies on the physiological and productive parameters of sheep raised under tropical conditions.

the results of this experiment show that there is a significant effect on the production and physiological parameters of lambs under thermal stress.

, under tropical conditions, the use of a complete diet (based on concentrate) is more effective than a semi-concentrate diet in terms of production parameters, and in terms of the physiological parameters of small ruminants, and the use of the semi-concentrate system is more effective than the complete concentrate system in terms of physiological parameters.

the results of this study showed that the use of a high fiber diet (HFD) in sheep, during the summer, is an effective strategy for reducing body temperature, and consequently, the physiological stress caused by the high ambient temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a high energy ration (H.E.R.) in the diet of sheep and goats under tropical conditions is a good management strategy.

the results of this experiment indicate that the use of a diet with a high level of crude protein (CP) and low fiber levels in sheep raised under tropical climate conditions is an efficient strategy for improving growth performance and physiological parameters associated with heat stress.
the use of the system of continuous grazing with access to water troughs, in the summer season, in a tropical climate, has no effect on the productive parameters of the lambs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of heat stress on small ruminants are complex and that a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms is needed to develop effective management practices to minimize the negative impact of heat stress on production and health of sheep and goats in tropical and subtropical regions.
